quests.name: The Relief of the Gate
quests.text: The Sentinel asked why no one came back for him. Lay him to rest, and gather what the Courtyard still records of his posting, so that someone can finally say he is relieved.
quests.done_text: "Sergeant. You are relieved." Nobody answers. Lyra is quiet for a while afterward.

quests.name: Older Than My Bloodline
quests.text: Orren wants proof that you are more than a thing the old kings left lying about. Walk the Courtyard, the Blackwood and the Citadel to their ends, and show him five sequences of the blade you found for yourself.
quests.done_text: Orren unrolls a bundle of his family's scraps on the anvil. "My grandmother called it prayer. It was a wiring diagram."

quests.name: What the Kings Bred
quests.text: The Huntsman has spent his life ending what the old kings bred. Put down the whelp in the Roost's boneyard and the drake on the Citadel's kennel stair, and he may believe you are not one of them.
quests.done_text: Two fresh marks are scored through on a strip of hide left where you would find it. Beside them, a purse, and no message.

quests.name: Six People I Buried
quests.text: She said you fight like six people she buried. Face her on the Cathedral steps, then walk the Sunken Crypt to its end, where the ones who made you left their names.
quests.done_text: Six names, said aloud in order. You knew each one before it was spoken.

quests.name: The Surviving Version
quests.text: History has been rewritten seventeen times. Recover thirty records from the road and the Archivist will have enough to state the one that was not.
quests.done_text: "Version zero. Not surviving. True. I had forgotten there was a difference."

quests.name: Names for the Waiting
quests.text: The keeper of the First Tomb learned every name he guarded. With him gone, go down to the Gallery of Names and take them back from the thing that is eating them.
quests.done_text: The lantern at the First Tomb burns a little higher. The names you carried up are said there now, by you.

quests.name: The Chain That Stayed
quests.text: Whatever is chained in the pit under the Citadel was told to stay, three hundred years ago, and has. Go down and end its waiting.
quests.done_text: "It waited all that time for someone to tell it otherwise," Lyra says. "I am glad it was not alone at the end."

quests.name: The Rain
quests.text: Lyra thinks she remembers rain, and does not know where she would have felt it. Follow the trail through the Cathedral, the Crypt and the Throne to learn where her mind is kept.
quests.done_text: Now you know where she is. "Tell me about it again," she says. "The rain. Slowly, this time."

side.name: Stock for the Anvil
side.text: Orren is low on sound metal. Bring him six pieces of Old Iron from the Courtyard or the Blackwood, and he will show you what his family did with the offcuts.
side.done_text: "Garrison stock. Rust on the outside, honest underneath." He rubs a rag of black oil along your vambrace without asking.

side.name: Proof Strokes
side.text: Orren has reground a Courtyard Longsword and does not trust his own work until it has been used in earnest. Win three fights with one in your hand.
side.done_text: He sights down the edge for a long time. "It held. Good. I was not sure I still could."

side.name: Silver for the Dead's Edge
side.text: Grave Silver takes an edge nothing else will. Bring Orren five pieces and he will finish a blade he has had on the bench since before you woke.
side.done_text: "There. It is not for sale to anybody. It is for sale to you." A long shape lies on the bench under a cloth.

side.name: Both Hands, Once
side.text: Orren says nobody understands a greatsword until it has nearly pulled them over. Win two fights with one.
side.done_text: "And now your shoulders know why I charge more for them."

side.name: As Far As It Goes
side.text: Take one blade as far as the forge can take it: every blade tier, the full grip, and a cored ore. Orren wants to see it finished, once, in his lifetime.
side.done_text: He holds it to the light and then hands it back hilt first. "My grandmother would have called that a prayer answered. I call it paid for."

side.name: Carry the Light
side.text: Somebody carried a sanctuary candle as far down as the unlit stair in the Deep. Lyra asks you to carry another there, so the first is not alone. Wear the Sanctuary Candle when you reach the Last Candle.
side.done_text: Two lights on the stair now. "Thank you," Lyra says. "I do not know why that mattered so much. I will think about why."

side.name: What the Courtyard Hid
side.text: Lyra's plans of the Fallen Courtyard are three hundred years out of date. Find three things there that are on no plan she holds.
side.done_text: "Three. On a ground I thought I knew stone by stone. I am going to have to look at everything again."

side.name: Stand Still
side.text: You walk through places as if they were only on the way. Lyra asks you, three times, somewhere on the road, simply to stay and listen until the place has finished speaking.
side.done_text: "You heard them. Most people leave before a place has finished."

side.name: Without a Mark
side.text: Lyra watches every blow that lands on you and can do nothing about any of them. Win three fights without being struck, as a kindness to her.
side.done_text: "Three times I did not have to look away. I had forgotten what that was like."

side.name: Count the Niches
side.text: There are more niches in the Sunken Crypt than the kingdom ever had dead. Recover every record the Crypt's road holds, so the count can be made properly.
side.done_text: Lyra reads the count back to you, slowly. It is not a number of graves. It is a number of people.

side.name: For the Record
side.text: The Witness wrote down what he was told to for a lifetime. Bring him ten things nobody told anyone to write down.
side.done_text: "Ten corrections. The record is still a disgrace, but it is now a disgrace with footnotes."

side.name: A Proper Answer
side.text: The Witness holds that a parry made at exactly the right moment is the only honest sentence in fencing. Make twenty-five of them.
side.done_text: "Twenty-five. I counted. It is what I do."

side.name: Two Tellings
side.text: The Witness will not say what you should do with the Crown. He would like to see, for the record, two of the things that can be done with it.
side.done_text: "I have now seen it end twice and neither was the one I was ordered to write. Good."

side.name: The Unscored Rows
side.text: Three rows on the Huntsman's tally were never scored through. Put down the knuckle-walker in the Blackwood, the crawler in the Crypt and the white beast of the Citadel's great stair. They are not always on the road: look for them.
side.done_text: You score the three rows through yourself. The knife is still sharp.

side.name: Answer the Roll
side.text: The muster nailed in the guardhouse lists five kinds of soldier 'posted'. Meet each of them once on the Courtyard's roads, so that somebody has answered the roll.
side.done_text: Five names answered. The ink of the sixth, the sergeant's, has not changed. It was never going to.

side.name: Ring It Where It Rang
side.text: The handbell the Beast kept was the choir-master's. Carry it back up to the Choir Loft, where the hymn is still running without him.
side.done_text: You ring it once. The recording falters for half a beat, as if somebody had looked up.
